gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-sundan: Expressive and wide-spaced, Bushcraft draws every curve at a single line width, so its capitals barely rise above the lowercase. And Noto Sans Sundanese sits beneath in open, low-slung sans-serif forms; keep its size modest so those crossbars stay easy to see.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-sunuwa: Bushcraft spaces its closed, cord-like letters far apart, with no modulation between stems and connecting strokes. Noto Sans Sunuwar is the one that opens its curves like a rope's bight, with short ascender stems on tall lowercase bodies.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-syloti: Noto Sans Syloti Nagri has short ascenders, a tall x-height and an a whose lower bowl opens up to breathe. And over a longer page it would read smoothly and cleanly, while Bushcraft's closed, widely spaced letters stay up top.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Rounded, bulb-like lowercase meets a stringlike heading. Over a longer page, Noto Sans Syriac would feel approachable and modern, its s shapes turning wide and easy, while Bushcraft sits above it in drawn-string lines.

Bushcraft draws every letter with one constant line width. Noto Sans Syriac Eastern carries a longer page comfortably, its tall lowercase standing against small caps and its curve endings never creeping toward each other.

Noto Sans Syriac Western reads modern and clean. Across a longer page its small letters stack up tall like bundled cable, terminals held well away from the stroke body, under Bushcraft's wire-thick, closed heading.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-tagalo: Noto Sans Tagalog reads with its middle zone dominating the line, and its curve gaps stay generous. But Bushcraft is the one for making an entrance, with closed, widely spaced letters, while the body font simply carries the text.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-tagban: Artistic and unhurried, Bushcraft strings its closed letters out with no vertical emphasis and no horizontal thinning. Then Noto Sans Tagbanwa follows with open curves and clear gaps, so a longer page feels clean, with lowercase filling most of the height.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Bushcraft's rounded strokes look like cut lengths of cord, closed and loosely spaced. Noto Sans Tai Le is the opposite quality in a plain sans, with ink strokes tapering out before they touch.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-tai-th: Bushcraft has no vertical emphasis and no horizontal thinning, just closed letters set far apart. Noto Sans Tai Tham, a plain sans, crowds its chalk-board lowercase toward the capital line, so a longer page reads dense yet open.
